notes:
Created TC-54484 (integer id 1985018) in project PR-2005 (379335744), folder __scratch__ (764138). Single attempt, 200 on the first try -- no retries needed.

JSON_PATH WRAPPER TRAP -- not encountered here, and that is itself the finding: describeCapability lists `test_case` as an explicit required BODY FIELD (an object), not as separate json_path display-only metadata layered over a flat body. Sent nested exactly as declared (`{test_case: {...}, folder_id: ...}`) and it worked immediately; no flat-vs-nested rejection to report. This capability's nesting is real, not cosmetic.

V1 TEMPLATE SUPPORT -- settled: v1 DOES support templates, contrary to the possibility that template selection is v2-only. Sending `test_case.template: "test_case_steps"` (the step-shaped template) was accepted and correctly switched the case onto that template: the response echoes template=test_case_steps, template_step_type=test_case_steps, template_name='Test Case Steps', template_id=1164, and the sent test_case_steps payload was actually stored (visible in test_case.test_case_steps, see below) -- it was not silently dropped. v1 does not ignore templates.

TEST_CASE_STEPS OBJECT-VS-ARRAY -- CONFIRMED on the write side. The contract's own declared 200 schema for `test_case.test_case_steps` is a single OBJECT with step-authoring fields (background, feature, hashed_id, scenario, sharedStep, shared_step_detail_id, shared_step_id, test_data, test_recording_id, title, plus id/order/project_id/result/step/updated_at/created_at). The live response instead returns an ARRAY of step records, and the items carry a materially different field set: present are id, step, result, order, project_id, updated_at, created_at (7 of the declared keys) plus three undeclared keys (record_status, group_id, test_case_id); absent are all 10 of the BDD/shared-step-authoring keys the declared object promises (background, feature, hashed_id, scenario, sharedStep, shared_step_detail_id, shared_step_id, test_data, test_recording_id, title). This is exactly the write-side half of the read-side `test_case_steps` object/array drift already seen on sibling read capabilities -- confirmed here on create_test_case_by_integer_id too. Separately, the contract's OTHER declared steps field, `test_case.steps` (an array of {step,result}), came back as an empty array `[]` even though steps were sent and did land in `test_case_steps` -- so `steps` is not where step data actually surfaces on this route; a caller reading only the declared `steps` field would conclude the case has no steps when it does.

DUPLICATE-ID BLOCK QUESTION -- this create settles it for THIS endpoint, in the 'both blocks are live' direction, not the 'one canonical' direction: priority/case_type/status were deliberately sent using the UPPER id block (318618/318626/318632) rather than the pool's known-good LOWER block (318591/318599/318605), and the response echoed back the exact SAME upper-block ids with correct, matching internal_name/name (Medium/Other/Active) -- the create did not reject the upper block, silently substitute the lower/canonical block, or produce any inconsistency between the id and its name/internal_name. That is one data point (single endpoint, single field set) toward 'both copies in a duplicate pair are equally live and interchangeable' rather than 'one is canonical and the other stale' -- consistent with, and now directly supporting from the write side, the open question raised by get_system_field_values's probe this session.

OTHER DRIFT: every one of the three option objects (case_type, priority, status) declares a `field_name` property that is never populated on any of the three -- it is simply absent, not null, on all three in this response. Each of the three also returns an undeclared `value_category` (null for case_type/priority, null for status too here since automation_state is the only field_name that populates it). `automation_state` is returned in full (id/internal_name/colour/value_category/name) alongside the declared `automation_status` ({name,value}) -- two different representations of the same underlying fact, only one of which is in the contract. `folder` and every `path_folders[]` entry carry several undeclared bookkeeping fields (notes, identifier, created_at/updated_at, deleted, parent_id, source, entity_type) beyond the declared folder-summary schema, mirroring the same 'the summary object is bigger in practice than declared' pattern seen elsewhere in this campaign.

Field-type note (not treated as drift): request-side `test_case.test_case_folder_id` is declared type `string` and was sent as `"764138"`; the response's `test_case.test_case_folder_id` is declared and returned as an `integer` (764138). The API accepts a numeric string on write and always serializes an integer on read -- consistent, not contradictory, but worth flagging since the two schemas use different types for the same logical field.

Not exercised in this probe: `create_at_root` (project already has folders, so this would 400 'Root Folder Already Exists' per the contract's own guidance -- not worth spending the write budget confirming an already-documented 400), `create_subfolder`/`scenario_name`, `shared_precondition_id`, `reviewers`/`review_status` e-signature gating (project has no stored project_settings, confirmed by this session's get_project_settings probe, so review-approve is off and that path is unreachable here), and `owner` non-membership fallback.
